```plato
    //==
    // # The expand, bevel and snub Archimedeans
    //
    // The six Archimedean solids the base catalog
    // could not name: the expand, bevel and
    // snub families, each a one-line Conway program
    // over a Platonic seed. Together
    // with the base catalog this names all thirteen Archimedeans.
    //
    // The `shrink` / `twist` constants below are the values that make each result
    // UNIFORM — every edge the same length (verified numerically to 1e-15 relative
    // spread). The expand shrinks have closed forms; the snub constants are the
    // roots of the usual snub polynomials (tribonacci-flavoured for the cube) and
    // are recorded as solved decimals. Twists are positive, picking the
    // counter-clockwise enantiomer of each chiral snub; negate them for the mirror.
    //
    // Bevel's vertex faces are rectangles rather than squares: topology and
    // planarity exact, edge lengths not all equal.

    //==
    // Expand family (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhombicuboctahedron).

    // 8 triangles + 18 squares on 24 vertices; uniform at shrink = sqrt(2) - 1.
    Rhombicuboctahedron(_: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMesh3D.Cube.Expand(Number.SqrtTwo - 1.0);

    // 20 triangles + 30 squares + 12 pentagons on 60 vertices; uniform at
    // shrink = phi / 3
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhombicosidodecahedron).
    Rhombicosidodecahedron(_: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMesh3D.Dodecahedron.Expand(Number.Phi / 3.0);

    //==
    // Bevel family (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Truncated_cuboctahedron).

    // 12 squares + 8 hexagons + 6 octagons on 48 vertices.
    TruncatedCuboctahedron(_: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMesh3D.Cube.Bevel;

    // 30 squares + 20 hexagons + 12 decagons on 120 vertices
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Truncated_icosidodecahedron).
    TruncatedIcosidodecahedron(_: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMesh3D.Dodecahedron.Bevel;

    //==
    // Snub family — chiral; these are the counter-clockwise enantiomers.

    // 32 triangles + 6 squares on 24 vertices; the twist is the classical
    // 16.4675 degrees (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snub_cube).
    SnubCube(_: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMesh3D.Cube.Snub(0.437593286000961, Angle(0.287413148757778));

    // 80 triangles + 12 pentagons on 60 vertices; the twist is the classical
    // 13.1064 degrees (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snub_dodecahedron).
    SnubDodecahedron(_: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMesh3D.Dodecahedron.Snub(0.562121964811048, Angle(0.228749892022033));

    //==
    // # Dual, ambo and truncate on polygon meshes
    //
    // The three core Conway polyhedron operators
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conway_polyhedron_notation) that generate the
    // catalog: applied to the Platonic seeds of the last section they produce the
    // Archimedean and Catalan solids that the catalog sections above name. The
    // expand, snub and bevel operators follow in the next section.
    //
    // Each operator is the same three lines — new positions, new faces around the
    // old faces, new faces around the old vertices — because the corner numbering
    // of `meshes-polygon.library.plato` already names every element the
    // operators need:
    //
    //   dual      one new vertex per FACE      (its centroid)
    //   ambo      one new vertex per EDGE      (its midpoint)
    //   truncate  one new vertex per CORNER    (a third of the way along its edge)
    //
    // So the new vertex numbering is just the face / edge / corner numbering, and
    // no lookup table is built anywhere.
    //
    // Precondition for all three: a closed manifold mesh with convex faces.
    //
    // NONE of them normalizes the result onto the unit sphere. That is deliberate:
    // pushing vertices out to a common radius is only meaning-preserving for a
    // VERTEX-transitive solid, and a Catalan dual is face-transitive instead — its
    // vertices genuinely sit at two or three different radii, so normalizing it
    // bends every face out of plane. Callers who know their result is
    // vertex-transitive (any Archimedean) can apply ProjectedToUnitSphere
    // themselves.
    // C# oracle: `Ara3D.Geometry.ConwayOperators` — but note the oracle normalizes
    // in all three operators and takes the vertex ring unreversed, so its duals come
    // out inside-out and its Catalan faces non-planar. The bodies below are the
    // corrected form, not a port of those two decisions.

    //==
    // Dual — vertices become faces and faces become vertices, so V and F swap
    // while E is unchanged (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dual_polyhedron).
    // Cube <-> octahedron, dodecahedron <-> icosahedron, tetrahedron is self-dual.

    // The outward unit normal of a face: its Newell vector area
    // (`polygons.library.plato`), normalized. Exact for a planar face,
    // and the least-squares plane normal of a nearly planar one.
    // Precondition: the face is non-degenerate.
    FaceUnitNormal(self: PolygonMesh3D, face: Integer): Vector3D
        => self.FacePositions(face).VectorArea.Normalize;

    // One dual vertex per face, placed by polar reciprocation about the unit
    // sphere: a face lying in the plane { x : x.n = d } (unit normal n, support
    // distance d = n.centroid) reciprocates to the point n / d
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dual_polyhedron#Polar_reciprocation). Every
    // dual face then lies in a plane by construction — all reciprocals of planes
    // through a point v lie in { x : x.v = 1 } — which is what keeps the Catalan
    // solids planar; the face centroids alone do not, and centroid / |centroid|^2
    // is only right when the centroid ray is perpendicular to the face (true for
    // a face with a symmetry axis, false for e.g. the edge-triangles of a snub).
    // Precondition: no face plane passes through the origin.
    PolarVertices(self: PolygonMesh3D): Array<Point3D>
        => self.FaceCount.MapRange(f =>
            (self.FaceUnitNormal(f)
                / self.FaceUnitNormal(f).Dot(self.FaceCentroid(f).PositionVector)).ToPoint);

    // The dual face of a vertex: the faces meeting at it, named by the dual
    // vertices they became. Taken in REVERSED rotation order — a face built
    // around a vertex winds opposite to the rotation that generated it, so
    // without the reversal every dual face points inward.
    DualFaceOfVertex(self: PolygonMesh3D, vertex: VertexIndex): Array<VertexIndex>
        => self.ReversedVertexCornerRing(vertex).Map(c => VertexIndex(self.CornerFace(c).Value));

    // One dual vertex per face, one dual face per vertex.
    Dual(self: PolygonMesh3D): PolygonMesh3D
        => PolygonMeshOfFaces(
            self.PolarVertices,
            self.VertexCount.MapRange(v => self.DualFaceOfVertex(VertexIndex(v))));

    //==
    // Ambo — rectification: cut each vertex back to the midpoints of its edges,
    // leaving one face per original face and one per original vertex, meeting at
    // one vertex per original edge (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rectification_(geometry)).
    // Cube -> cuboctahedron, dodecahedron -> icosidodecahedron.

    // The midpoint of every undirected edge, in edge-index order: the vertices
    // of the ambo. Folded over the corners in ascending order keeping only the
    // canonical half of each twin pair — whose rank IS its edge index, so the
    // result lands in CornerUndirectedEdge order by construction. `Repeat(0, …)` is the
    // empty seed.
    UndirectedEdgeMidpoints(self: PolygonMesh3D): Array<Point3D>
        => self.CornerCount
            .MapRange(c => CornerIndex(c))
            .Reduce(Repeat(0, Point3D.Origin),
                (acc, c) => self.IsCanonicalCorner(c) ? acc.Append(self.CornerLerp(c, 0.5)) : acc);

    // The shrunken copy of an original face: its own edges' midpoints, in order.
    AmboFaceOfFace(self: PolygonMesh3D, face: Integer): Array<VertexIndex>
        => self.FaceArity(face).MapRange(slot =>
            VertexIndex(self.CornerUndirectedEdge(self.FaceCorner(face, slot)).Value));

    // The face left where a vertex was: the midpoints of the edges meeting at
    // it. Taken in reversed rotation order so it winds counter-clockwise seen
    // from outside, like the faces it neighbours.
    AmboFaceOfVertex(self: PolygonMesh3D, vertex: VertexIndex): Array<VertexIndex>
        => self.ReversedVertexCornerRing(vertex).Map(c => VertexIndex(self.CornerUndirectedEdge(c).Value));
```
